paper_metadata.title: Effect of Nb on Mechanical Properties of HAZ for High-Nb X80 Pipeline Steels
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Iron and Steel Research, International

evidence.quote: the mechanical properties of heat affected zone (HAZ) of two commercial high-Nb X80 grade pipeline steels with different alloy elements were investigated using thermal simulation
the effectsof the types of microstructures formed in the HAZ thermal cycles on the toughness of HAZ for TMCp steels with compositions similar to those used in this work

For steel A, the low-temperature impact toughness of HAZ of the steel pipe was higher, and few bending cracks occurred in HAZ, whereas for steel B, the probabilities of occurrence of low-impact toughness and bending cracks were higher than those of Steel A.

evidence.quote: Weld thermal simulation was carried out on a Gleeble 3500 thermomechanical simulator to study the microstructure evolution and mechanical properties changes in coarse grain heat affected zone (CGHAZ)
high strength and high toughness steel plates can be manufactured by TMCP (Table 2).
The microstructure of Steel A mainly consists of acicular ferrite [Fig. 1(a)], consisting of some fine quasi-polygonal ferrites and dark-island constituents
consisting of some fine quasi-polygonal ferrites and dark-island constituents
the dark-island constituents are considered as martensite/austenite (M/A) constituents
although the microstructure of Steel B displays main acicular ferrite microstructure characteristics, the sizes of ferrite and M/A constituents are large
At high peak temperature of 1350 ℃, the microstructure was mainly composed of granular bainite
plenty of dot-like or rod-like M/A constituents were distributed in the matrix
prior-austenite grain boundary (GB) was clearly visible
At high peak temperature of 1350 ℃, the microstructure was mainly composed of granular bainite
When the peak temperature decreased to 1000-900 ℃, the microstructure appeared to be dominated by quasi-polygonal ferrite
the M/A constituents are hard and brittle particles usually regarded as the site of crack initiation
under higher heat input conditions, coarse bainite is obtained in Steel B, resulting in lower toughness of HAZ for Steel B than for Steel A.

With the decrease in peak temperature, the microstructures of HAZs change from bainite to acicular ferrite, and the amount and size of the M/A constituents decrease, causing decrease in strength and increase in toughness.
